answer.rationale: The primary contract ends in 14 days with no auto-renew while the line is at 94% and has no buffer, so the single decision must keep supply continuous. Switching or standing up a second source would spend that slot on a transition the current buffer cannot absorb; deferral was only shown to work for a non-critical month-to-month case. Incumbent continuity has previously avoided integration and delivery breaks. The cost mandate is therefore pursued by renegotiating the incumbent at renewal—benchmarking and a longer volume term—rather than changing the source. Whether that path can deliver a full 18% spend cut is still unknown.
